ci._note: The home page runs two WebGL layers. On a GPU they are free — an unthrottled local run scores 1.00 with LCP ~325ms. On a CI runner there is no GPU, so Chrome rasterises in software and each full-viewport frame costs ~150ms, which Lighthouse attributes to the script and scores 0.60. That is a property of the measuring environment, not of the page: the drawArrays self-time across a whole load is 11ms. It cannot be gated away either — failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat REJECTS under an explicit --use-gl=swiftshader (what the e2e suite must use to have any GL at all) and ACCEPTS under CI's implicit software fallback, and the renderer string is identical in both, so any check that spares CI also disables the shaders in our own tests. Performance is therefore a warning here and an error everywhere else; accessibility stays an error on every page.
